top.para: Founders with years of checklists build the apps; villager services release them unchanged but deployed, locked down, tested and private where needed; users pay for use, explorers buy finite packs and sell it; the service becomes a commodity.

in-short.para: The brief; product managers; non-functional requirements; villager services; use and packs; they sell; our agents scale it.

brief.para: A checklist refined for ten years, a standard operating procedure with the important steps in bold: battle-hardened, and the valuable part.

explorers.para: Experienced, close to the problem, never needing GitHub, CI or tests, and certain to hit every non-functional requirement because the loop is addictive.

villagers.para: Release without changing functionality: a repository, deployment, review, tests and CI, passkey-private data in vaults, contained agents; on primitives that now exist, with a model account as the brain.

money.para: Users pay for use after the value, and for a vault; explorers buy finite packs of about £500, £2,000 or £5,000 with revenue share; and they sell it to their own community.

finite.para: Deliver a pack and hand it over; our own agents make each one faster, which is how it scales and what consulting becomes.

market.line: Who it is for, and how it spreads
market.para: Generation X founders with a running business; one person, then a second using what the first built; twenty people, twenty apps, none of which they want to maintain.

town.para: Clear packs, prices and a buy-now page, so the villager service is a commodity bought without a conversation.

limits.para: A proposal, nothing sold; participants unnamed; the primitives run in part; my interest.

sources.para: My voice memo of 31 October, after the Vibathon conversation.
